## Design hard rules — never violate these

- **Colored borders are allowed.** (Updated 2026-07-19 — reverses the earlier blanket ban.) Colored borders on cards/sections/elements are fine.
- **Side/left accent bars only on square-cornered elements.** A colored left/side accent stripe (`border-l-4`, etc.) is OK **only when the element has no border-radius**. Never put a side accent bar on a rounded (`rounded-*`) element — a colored bar clashing with a rounded corner is the look to avoid. Dots, icons, and background tints remain good status signals but are no longer mandatory substitutes.
- **Selected toggles are gray-900 (light) / gray-100 (dark), always — not blue, not the theme's primary orange.** (2026-09-02, DESIGN PASS 2.) Blue is `Deploying`'s colour and a toggle deploys nothing. Shipped on the History tab's Compare namespace / Show environments switch and the Logs tab's `Pods|Tests` switch and Follow/Wrap. `.btn-primary` is a SEPARATE decision: it is `blue-700` in `app.css`, which supersedes an older "primary button is gray-900" sentence still sitting in `frontend/DESIGN.md`'s "Buttons — 3 kinds" section — `app.css` is the later ruling, do not "fix" `Deploy` back to gray. The gray-900/white inversion survives for toggles and for the loud-by-contrast `default`/`ghost` button trick; it is gone only from the one filled PRIMARY action.
- **A region that reads as a destination must BE one.** (2026-09-01, from the human: *"it's also not clickable in places where you'd expect it to be. i think some other views have this problem too."*) A card header carrying an object's name, or a list row with a hover fill, is an affordance; if only a few characters of it navigate, it is a broken one.
  - The pattern is `.tap-zone` / `.tap-link` in `app.css`. The region gets `.tap-zone`, the ONE anchor that owns its primary destination gets `.tap-link`, and that anchor's `::after` covers the region. Every other control inside is raised above the overlay automatically and stays clickable.
  - **Never wrap the region in an `<a>`.** It nests interactive elements inside the row's existing links and buttons, which is invalid and doubles the tab stops.
  - `Card` takes `titleHref` for the header case.
  - The trade: text inside a tap zone is not selectable except inside the raised controls. Do not put one around prose meant to be copied.
- **`.tap-link` is class-based, so the primary control does not have to be an `<a>`.** A `<button>` takes it too, which is how rollout detail's `/history` rows keep click-to-expand instead of becoming a navigation.
- **Applied:** `/environments` card headers and app rows, `/envs/<name>` "Running now" rows, `/activity` event rows, `/namespaces/<name>` rollout rows, `ActivityRail` rows, `/versions` list rows (live, no-longer-running **and** never-deployed), rollout detail `/history` rows, `/apps` app rows. **Still unfixed:** none known. `/`, `/rollouts`, `/apps/<name>`'s commit spine and `/dependencies` are already whole-block anchors and are fine.
- **Three hand-rolled overlays were found and replaced, each broken a different way** — an `after:absolute after:inset-0` pair drawing its ring inside a `truncate` box (`overflow:hidden` clips it on all four sides), and twice an invisible `<a class="absolute inset-0">` with an `aria-label`, i.e. a focus ring around an unreadable rectangle. If you are about to write one, use `.tap-zone`.
- **A `role="button"` wrapper around a row that contains links is a keyboard bug, not just a semantics one.** On `/history` it swallowed Enter: the keydown bubbled from the version link to the wrapper's handler, which called `preventDefault()` and cancelled the link's own activation. The link had a `stopPropagation` workaround; both are gone.
- **The rank badge is COLOURED on both halves, and the deviation channel is HUE.** (2026-09-02, from the human: *"i thought about newest / behind badges to use more prominent colors, not these faint / no colors."* Fourth ruling in the same direction.) Measured on `DESIGN.md`'s own `area × chroma` formula, canvas-resolved against the composited card on `/rollouts` at 1440, the wash/block pair that shipped that morning scored **24.8 / 26.3 light and 66.8 / 65.6 dark — 1.06× and 0.98×**: the deviation was not louder than the norm on the colour instrument at all, only DARKER. For scale the quietest identity chip on the same row, `DEV`, scores 54.9.
  - **⛔ THE FIRST ATTEMPT SHIPPED AS TEAL + `blue-800` AND LASTED AN HOUR.** The human named both faults on sight: *"why is behind purple? and why is newest this weird tint and not plain green?"* Measured, both are exact: `teal-700` is OKLCH **h 186.4°** against plain green's **150.1°** — the word was **36° toward cyan** — and Tailwind's `blue` ramp is violet-leaning (`blue-800` **h 265.6° at C 0.199**), which at chip scale reads purple. **A hue nobody can name cannot carry a meaning.** Both had been arrived at by DODGING an adjacency rather than designing one.
  - `newest`/`head` → **`green-800` on `green-50`** / `green-300` on `green-950/30`. Plain green. The hand-picked `#426d64` / `#83b0a8` are retired.

Green is `newest`'s, red is adverse and behind is not adverse, amber IS `stuck`, violet is STAGING and cyan is TEST. Orange at h ~70° is what remains, and the human proposed it unprompted.

WEIGHT ANSWERS "HOW LOUD".** Being behind is a MEASUREMENT, not a verdict — drift is the pipeline's normal state, so most rollouts are behind most of the time, and what makes it matter is *why* (stuck, blocked, waiting), which already owns amber and red.
  - **A filled slate slab measured better than everything else and was still wrong** (3.84× the norm on weight, a 3.43× alarm lead on chroma). Measuring well is not the same as being right — look at it.

Two candidates died here: **`orange-900` ink is dE00 4.5 from `PROD`'s `amber-900` ink** (they are adjacent halves of one box on `/apps` — the collision that moved `rank` off amber originally), and **`orange-300` as a ground scores 242.2 on `area × chroma`, louder than `alarm` itself**; `orange-200` reads as amber-that-is-not-stuck when screenshotted beside a real `STUCK` chip.

  - ⚠️ **Honest residue:** `newest`'s `green-50` fill is dE00 **1.5** from the `DEV` chip's surface — they share a ground, and only the border (`gray-200` hairline vs `green-300` ring), the ink lightness and the word separate them. Do NOT "fix" it by deepening the fill: `green-100` measures presence 106 against `N behind`'s 154 and collapses the deviation ratio to 1.37×.
  - `failing`/`diverged`/`blocked` → light ground stepped **`red-50` → `red-100`**, because a merely-trailing chip must not out-ink a diverged one. Dark unchanged (`red-950/50`; its contrast argument still holds).

Shipped 1.41× light / 1.70× dark on chroma, 1.65× / 1.28× on `area × (chroma + |ΔL|)`. The 2.05× the blue pair reached was only available because that pair out-inked `diverged`, which is worse. A future pass wanting a bigger ratio must move `newest` down or `adverse` up — not this chip.
  - Adjacency, canvas-resolved: `newest` vs DEV ink **9.9 light / 9.1 dark**, vs the `Succeeded` disc **9.9 / 8.5** — both of those are DISCS or bordered identity chips, not rank chips.

  - **THE BORDER STAYS NEUTRAL ON EVERY NON-`env` ROLE.** Identity is a coloured EDGE; rank is a coloured FIELD inside the same `gray-200`/`gray-700` hairline `.chip-value` draws. Rendered with matching teal/blue borders instead, the joined badge reads as two glued boxes and a rank chip becomes indistinguishable in KIND from `[DEV]`.

- **`.chip`'s `12ch` cap was never twelve characters — it is 8.5.** (2026-09-02, third truncation report in one day: `STAGING 15 BEHI…` on `/versions/<rev>`.) `max-width: 12ch` resolves to **72.25px**; padding + border take 13.8 and one character costs 6.85 (1ch 6.02 + 0.8 letter-spacing), so the word's real budget is **(72.25 − 13.8) / 6.85 = 8.5 characters**. Every nine-character label has always clipped, and the fix had been applied three times as a per-call-site `wide`.
  - The cap is **per KIND of label** now, not per call site. `env` labels are UNBOUNDED (an environment, service or region name) and keep 12ch exactly — every deliberate "NOT `wide`" decision in `Navbar`, `CommandPalette` and `/environments` is byte-identical. Every other role's label comes from a CLOSED vocabulary whose longest member is `NEVER DEPLOYED` (109.5px bare, 123.5 with the tag), so the cap is **`calc(14ch+26px)` = 110.3px**, or `calc(14ch+40px)` when the tag draws.
  - It is **strictly tighter than `wide`**, which is what makes it safe across pages a pass does not own: no call site can render wider than an already-shipped `wide` chip. The `wide`s added for this bug are now redundant, not wrong.
  - A DEV `console.error` fires if a non-`env` label exceeds 14 characters, so the next one is NAMED instead of silently truncated.
  - Verified: every word in the vocabulary (`NEWEST`, `1/15/199 BEHIND`, `UNKNOWN`, `HELD`, `PENDING`, `PINNED`, `UNRELEASED`, `ROLLED BACK`, `NEVER DEPLOYED`, `DIVERGED`) renders unclipped with no horizontal overflow on 9 routes × 1440 and 390.

Measured canvas-resolved on the running product, the gray spelling sat **4.1°** of hue from `N behind` in light and **2.8°** in dark — i.e. the two members of the rank vocabulary were the same hue — while mint separates them by **81°**. `TONE.head` now resolves to `MINT_QUIET`; the role name survives only because four call sites are in files that pass did not own. **Do not give `head` a value of its own again.** Migrate those call sites to `role="newest"` and delete the entry.

Never delete the `h1` element itself — the skip link and the heading-structure tests need it.

A control that changes CLUSTER STATE is an ACTION and earns a `.btn`; a FILLED `.btn-primary` is reserved for the action that changes WHAT IS RUNNING, at most one per page.   - The pattern is a **query param naming the entry**, resolved in an `$effect` off `page.url.searchParams` — `?deploy=<revision>` on the History tab, the same shape as `/apps/<name>`'s `?release=<env>`, the logs tab's `?tab=`, `/activity`'s `?env=`. **Not a fragment**: a hash makes the browser scroll on its own, and on a list that renders after its query resolves that scroll lands at an offset that is wrong 300ms later and then visibly fights the page's own `scrollIntoView`.

  - **The graph inside the card was drawn NARROW, not small, and no fit can rescue that.** 571px of drawing centred in a 988px canvas **at scale 1.0**, 209px of empty ground a side. dagre was handed a FIXED `ranksep`, so a small graph is intrinsically narrow at every frame width. ⛔ **Do not reach for the zoom cap.** `maxZoom: 1` is on record in `GraphCanvasInner`: without it the same two-service graph came back at **1.6×**, printing a 13px node title at 21px. Raising it trades this defect for the one that rule exists to prevent.
  - **The fix is `fillWidth` on `GraphCanvas`: lay out once to learn the natural extent, then re-lay-out with the horizontal gutter widened by the shortfall.** ⭐ ONE RULE, BOTH ORIENTATIONS: **only the separation running along the frame's CONSTRAINED axis stretches**, and the card is width-bounded and height-derived at every width — so it is `ranksep` under `LR` (ranks are columns) and `nodesep` under `TB` (ranks are rows, the within-rank axis is horizontal). Nothing stretches vertically, which is the answer to *"does the card get taller"*: `frameHeight` is `contentHeight + 16`, so there was never any vertical slack — 20px of ground above and below against 209 on each side. Spreading rows would INVENT height and spend the axis that grows with the fleet to fix a defect on the axis that does not. **The card's height is identical before and after.**
  - **The cap: a graph may not be more gap than graph.** The gutters may never total more than the ranks they separate — at least half the stretched extent is ink. The budget is the drawing's own (`natural.width` minus the base gutters IS the summed rank width), so no magic multiplier, it self-scales with the node boxes, and it tightens as ranks are added, which is exactly when the drawing needs less help. Unbounded, the two-column tab wanted **582px** of nothing between two 220px boxes; past some width extra room is better left as MARGIN, outside the drawing, where it reads as the card breathing rather than as distance between two services.
  - Measured, 1800 → after: rollout tab **564→936 drawn in a 990→1198 canvas, 213→131px margins, zoom 1.0 both**; `/dependencies` **927→1069 in 1198, 146→77px**; **canvas height unchanged on both**. At 390 (`TB`) both already overflow, so both are byte-identical.
  - ⛔ **A drawing that already overflows is left entirely alone** — the predicate is *fits on the FREE axis*. On a 40-service × 4-environment fixture the frame is `maxHeight` and the fit lands on `minZoom`, so the frame is not what bounds the drawing; without that guard the arithmetic still found 14px to share out and spent a second dagre pass on 160 nodes to move four columns by 5px, rendered at 0.55. Verified identical with the stretch on and off: `1117×4104` content, zoom 0.55, 4 ranks, controls + minimap + pan on, same resting pan.
  - ⚠️ **Residue:** a drawing with ONE rank (the `/dependencies` env filter down to a single environment) has no gutter to widen and still centres in the card. That is honest — you cannot stretch a single column — but it is the one shape this rule cannot help.

- **An icon on this product is STRUCTURAL, and a mark that is not true of its kind is worse than no mark.** (2026-09-02, from the human on the gate row: *"still don't like these details when we have this nonsense icon. i feel like you could better visualize this rather than just putting ascii icons in there."*) Two of `BlockingStoryLines`' five marks were decoration, and one of them was a lie.
  - `HourglassSolid` over a `check` gate meant *time will fix this* — which is `clock`'s meaning, and `check` is defined as the kind that is NOT on a clock ("not passing, and nothing published a window"). **Two kinds may not share one meaning.** → `ShieldCheckSolid`.
  - `ArrowRightAltSolid` over `upstream` was a bare DIRECTION naming no object, and it stood for TWO mechanisms at once. Split by `kind`: a cross-service contract takes `ShareNodesSolid` (the mark `contractBlockReason` and `/dependencies` already spend on it), a promotion order takes `ChevronDoubleRightOutline` (the `Promotion pipeline` card header's). The calendar, the person and the question mark were already true and did not move.
  - **The mark is a function of `kind` first and `clears` second** — `clears` is the REMEDY, `kind` is the OBJECT, and an icon names an object. `gateMark()` is exported so the choice is arguable in a test rather than buried in markup. ⚠️ **It lives in `GateRecord.svelte`'s module script since 2026-09-02, not `BlockingStoryLines`'** — the record it belongs to is drawn at two scales now, and `BlockingStoryLines` imports it, so exporting from there and importing back would be a cycle.
- **A sentence that carries three facts with an obvious shape must be DRAWN, and then the sentence GOES.** *"Waiting for hello-api-app to ship a newer api — it is on 1.66.0"* is a provider, a contract with a required range, and the version it serves. It is now `⇄ hello-api-app [API|1.66.0] → [^1.67.0]` — `Chip`'s joined form for the caption+identifier pair, its identifier-only form for the requirement, and an arrow BETWEEN TWO OPERANDS (which is what separates a structural mark from a decorative one). The required range is `RolloutDependency.status.blockedReleases[].requiredVersion`; it has always been in the payload and nothing drew it.
  - ⛔ **Do not add a second graphic beside the sentence.** One fact drawn twice is the defect this branch has paid for repeatedly. Where the drawing carries the fact, `short` moves into the record behind the control.
  - ⛔ **And only where there IS a shape.** `check`, `approval` and `unknown` name no second party; their only concrete object is the gate's generated id, which was deliberately taken out of the printed tier. `blocking-story.ts` sets `subject: null` for those and the row prints `short`, unchanged. **Prose is what you use when you have no shape; it is not a failure to use it where there is none.**
  - ⛔ **Never draw half a relation.** No `providedVersion`, or two held candidates asking for different ranges (semver constraints are not orderable across spellings) → `need` is null and the sentence prints. A window with no `nextTransition` draws nothing either: a NAME is not a state, and `reopens in` with no clock after it is a broken sentence.
  - `subject` + `predicate` are `clause` SPLIT AT ITS OWN JOINT and `clause` is rebuilt from them, so the drawn row and the banner sentence cannot drift.
- **A disclosure whose payoff is a paragraph is the weakest one there is; a RECORD gets a popover.** (2026-09-02, from the human: *"i think i also don't like 'details' expansion. it's formatted just as text when in some cases it could be more richly formatted. i think maybe a popover would be better?"*) `RulePopover.svelte` holds one aligned `<dl>` block per gate — the rule's own name, `Kind`, `Clears`, `When`, `Rule` (and `Status` for the controller enum).
  - ⛔ **IT IS STILL A NATIVE `<details>`, AND THAT IS NOT AN IMPLEMENTATION DETAIL.** flowbite's `<Popover>` renders `{#if isOpen}` — **a closed one has no DOM.** `lib/messages/` pins these sentences by walking `textContent`, so swapping it in would have made every fact unreachable to the census WHILE THE SUITE STAYED GREEN — the exact failure `AlertPanel.svelte.test.ts` exists to catch. Its default `trigger="hover"` is the second reason: unreachable on a phone.
  - The `<details>` gives keyboard (a `<summary>` is focusable, Enter/Space activate), touch (a tap is a click) and `details.open` as a testable boolean for free. Escape, click-away and focus return are twenty lines on top. Verified at 1440 and 390.
  - ⚠️ **`position: fixed`, never `absolute`.** `Card.svelte` is `overflow-hidden`, so an absolutely positioned panel is clipped at the card's edge on `/environments`, `/apps/<name>` and `/envs/<name>`. Coordinates are measured off the summary, flipped above when the viewport is short, clamped to 8px gutters.
  - **THE RECORD HOLDS WHAT THE ROW DOES NOT.** A row that printed `short` does not get a `Clears` row too — opening a control to read a sentence already on screen is the complaint that produced this pass.
  - The control reads **`1 rule` / `N rules`** in BOTH card-scale components now. `BlockingStoryLines` said `Details` and `BlockReason` said the count form, one viewport apart on `/environments` — one affordance, two grammars. ~~`AlertPanel`'s own `Details` is untouched: its body is a SENTENCE, not a set with a count.~~ **Superseded the same day — see the next entry. That argument was true of SOME of `AlertPanel`'s ten call sites and false of others, and leaving it produced a THIRD collapse of the same vocabulary.**

- **⭐ THE TRIGGER GRAMMAR IS `lib/disclosure.ts` NOW, AND IT IS ABOUT THE CONTENT, NOT ABOUT THE COMPONENT.** (2026-09-02, from the human: *"there are few more 'details' that have not been redesigned."*) The label had collapsed twice — five question shapes → `Details`/`1 rule`, then card-scale `N rules` against banner-scale `Details` on the same gates 90px apart on `/environments` — because the grammar lived at the CALL SITES. It is one function and one rule:
  - **A SET you can count, of one kind** → **`N <noun>`** (`1 rule`, `3 rules`, `2 services`, `1 contract`). `AlertPanel` takes `footnoteCount` + `footnoteNoun`; `RulePopover` takes `count` + `noun`; both call `countLabel`. **The count form applies at n = 1 too** — a one-gate banner and a two-gate banner must not read as different KINDS of control.
  - **ONE RECORD with fields** → **`Details`**. ⛔ NOT `1 request`: a count of one over a thing there can only ever be one of is pedantry and teaches nothing. The record's shape is carried by the `<dl>`, not by the word in front of it.
  - **A GENUINE SENTENCE** → **`Details`**, unchanged, and still the honest default. Where there is no shape, prose is correct and a count would be a lie.
  - ⛔ Still no verbs, no interrogatives, no claims. A label states the KIND of thing behind the control.
- **AND THE BODY BEHIND IT HAS THREE SHAPES, NOT ONE.** (2026-09-02) `AlertPanel`'s `footnote` was a `string` on all ten callers, so a SET and a MACHINE RECORD were both being narrated as prose. `footnoteBody` is the record slot; `FactList.svelte` is the product's ONE aligned `<dl>` (10px uppercase `t-label` against 11px `t-micro`, `auto 1fr`) and `GateRecord.svelte` is the gate-shaped one that BOTH the banner and the card popover render.
  - **`FactList`'s `tone="banner"` reads `currentColor`** off `AlertPanel`'s footnote class, so the record speaks in the severity's ink like the `Details` summary above it and the `.nav-link` beside it. ⚠️ Label and value get the SAME ink there, deliberately: the panel's palette note records that NO alpha clears 4.5:1 over its gradient in light, so the ladder is carried by SIZE and CASE.
  - **A `<dt>` over a sentence is prose wearing a label, and is banned.** The verdict/`resolution`/`rollbackNext` line stays a `<p>` under a hairline; only fields get labels.
  - ⛔ **THE RECORD HOLDS WHAT THE HOST DOES NOT PRINT.** `GateRecord`'s `clearsFor` is a callback for exactly this: the CARD row draws its clause so `short` belongs in the record, but a gate with no `subject` prints `short` and must not get it twice; the BANNER prints `consequence`, which already carries every gate's clause, so no gate gets a `Clears` row there at all.
  - ⚠️ **A snippet reference is always truthy**, so `footnoteBody` is passed CONDITIONALLY (`gates.length ? gateBody : undefined`). Handing one over unconditionally gives the panel a body it must render, and an empty record behind a labelled control is the empty disclosure `AlertPanel.svelte.test.ts` forbids.
  - ⚠️ **No nested template literals in a `.ts` fact value.** `` `${a}${x ? ` · ${x}` : ''}` `` comes back to `lib/messages/scan.ts`'s regex as the fragment `…${until ?` — a census entry nobody can read, for a message that does not exist. Build the parts first.
- **THE CALLER-BY-CALLER CLASSIFICATION, so the next pass does not re-derive it.** (2026-09-02)
  - **SET → count.** `BlockingStoryPanel` (reaches `/apps`, `/environments`, `/apps/<name>`, rollout detail) `N rules`; `/envs/<name>`'s blocked banner `N rules` — **that call site was still `Which rule` / `Which rules`, an interrogative the ban a day earlier never reached**; `/versions` and `/versions/<rev>` `N rules`; the dependencies tab `N contracts` (blocked-by) and `N services` (holding).
  - **MACHINE FACT → fields, `Details`.** `ErrorState` (`errorDetail` → `errorFacts`: `Address` / `Status` / `Server said`); `+error.svelte` (`Address` / `Status`); rollout detail's and the History tab's 404 (`Rollout` / `Cluster` / `Server answered`); `/apps`' failed-deploy (`Last attempt`); rollout detail's rollback (`Rolled back by`) and pin (`Pinned by`), whose sentences stay printed as sentences.
  - **GENUINE SENTENCE → `Details`, unchanged.** Rollout detail's `Automatic deploys are paused` (`A deploy you start by hand still applies immediately.`), `FailurePanel`, `ScheduleStatus`, `/apps`' pin banner, `/apps/<name>`'s pin and stuck banners, `/activity` (`Press Failed below to see all N.`). None of these names a second party or has a count; prose is what you use when there is no shape.

- **A gate belongs on the HOP, not in a card beside the chain — and a hop that carries nothing is the chain's biggest empty.** (2026-09-02, from the human on `/apps/<name>`: *"the hop between stations, which is where the gate actually lives, carries nothing"* — each station row was `[DEV] [1 BEHIND 2.66.0-66] …600px… 2d ago`.) A station answers *what runs here*; the HOP is the promotion, so the thing refusing a promotion is drawn on it. `PromotionPipeline`'s `Hop` takes a `story` and renders `BlockingStoryLines` — **imported, never restated**, so the clause on the edge and the clause on `/environments` are one object.
  - ⭐ **THE EDGE INTO THE FIRST STAGE IS A HOP AND HAD NO OBJECT.** With every environment on one build, every edge BETWEEN stations is in sync and the only thing held is the newest build's entry into DEV. `entryHop` renders ONLY when held — an open entry hop is the norm, and `.pp--entry` then drops `pp-front`'s bottom hairline so the rail is the single separator that carries meaning.
  - ⛔ **ONE CAUSE IS DRAWN ONCE, ON THE MOST UPSTREAM EDGE IT BITES**, and skipped on the contiguous run below it. One dependency gate holding DEV, STAGING and PROD drawn per station is the same clause three times — the repetition rule that folded `Needs you` to one row. WHO it holds is the BANNER's job.
  - ⛔ **AND ONLY CAUSES NOBODY ELSE IS DRAWING.** The set is exactly `waitGroups` — blocks that carry NO control. A gate needing a person is a `decision` with a `Deploy` button beside it; its edge still goes DASHED (the shape says *held*) but the clause is not repeated. Every cause an edge draws is struck from `Waiting, nothing to do` (`hopCauseKeys`), which on `hello-frontend-app` empties the card and the whole act column.
  - **THE RECORD FOLLOWS THE DRAWING.** With the gate on the edge, `› 1 rule` rendered TWICE in one viewport — banner and hop. `BlockingStoryPanel`'s `showRules={false}` exists for exactly this (*"off where the surround already draws them"*); the banner keeps its verdict sentence. Hide it ONLY when the two records would be the same set, i.e. the banner's story has no `promotion` gate the narrowed hop story lacks.
  - The row is a `.tap-zone` to the PROVIDER, with a chevron as the one `.tap-link`. **Not the provider's name** — the clause 8px left already prints it at full ink.
- **A banner headlining ONE environment when one cause holds N is the loudest object on the page naming the smallest part of its subject.** (2026-09-02) `blockedEnv` picks who to speak FOR; the SCOPE is a separate page-level decision. `blockingStory`'s `subject` option is the lever — no classifier change. The subject must be grammatically **singular** (`${subject} is waiting on …` is owned by `blocking-story.ts`), so it is `hello-frontend-app in all 3 environments`, which is `/apps`' own already-shipped spelling (`hello-frontend-app in DEV is …`) generalised from one environment to the set. ⛔ **Never said of one**: a single held environment keeps bare `place`, or the app's name on the app's own page is spent for nothing.
- **A rail that empties exactly when the app is worst is backwards.** (2026-09-02) `/apps/<name>`'s rail was `Source` alone (the exposure card needs pod counts the managed-resources call cannot always resolve), so the column beside the page's lead object was 340px of nothing on the one app that was stuck. It carries `How it's going` now — the SAME card `/apps` and `/envs/<name>` hold in the same slot, third page in a family of three. ⛔ **`Furthest behind` — the row both siblings carry third — is deliberately absent**: every station prints its own `N behind` chip 300px left. ⛔ **And the lead time is a ROW, not the rollup**: as a rollup it printed `—` in the header on every app whose retained history has not carried one build the whole way, and a card whose one-glance answer is an em dash has no answer. The rollup is the cadence (sparkline + `N in 7d`); an em dash belongs where a label beside it says what could not be measured.

- **A `dd` HOLDS ONE FIGURE; A SECOND OBJECT BELONGS ON THE LABEL SIDE.** (2026-09-02.) `/apps`' `How it's going` rail printed `Furthest behind` … `hello-frontend-app 1` — a mono identifier flush against a bare digit, which reads as a name with a stray number rather than as one fact. The digit was never the problem: `32` and `9h` take their meaning from their label the same way. The intruder was a SECOND OBJECT in the value cell that the other two rows do not have. The app name moved into the `<dt>` (`Furthest behind hello-frontend-app`), so all three `dd`s are one 16px tabular figure sharing one right-hand column. ⚠️ `Deploys · 7d`'s sparkline is not a counter-example — it is the SAME figure drawn over time, not a second value. `whitespace-nowrap` stays on the WORDS only and the name `truncate`s: a 40-character name keeps the row at 24px and the figure on the edge.
- **A CLUSTER OF MARKS ON A TIME AXIS IS ONE MARK THAT SAYS HOW MANY.** (2026-09-02.) `/activity` declines `DeploymentTimeline`'s vertical fan for a good reason (a lane is a whole environment; eight builds in a minute become a bead-chain that reads as if height meant something) — but declining it left `●◗` amoebas that are neither one mark nor two, and at a 7-day scale collisions are the RESTING STATE, not an edge case. A run of marks inside `MIN_SEP` now draws one larger disc at the run's centre with the count inside it, in the run's WORST status ink so a merged mark can never hide a failure.
  - ⛔ **IT REPLACES NOTHING IN THE DOM.** Every member keeps its own `<circle>` at its own x, its `aria-label`, its place in the roving tabindex and its handlers; members are only made INVISIBLE. ⚠️ **And `pointer-events="all"` with it — a `fill: transparent` circle is not a PAINTED one, so under SVG's default `visiblePainted` it stops receiving hover and the bubble becomes a dead zone.**
  - The bubble hides while any member is hovered, focused or selected, so a pointer moving across it RESOLVES it into the deploy underneath and `←`/`→` still walk every mark. Verified on the live page: 47 dots, 47 accessible names, 3 tab stops (one per lane), 7 bubbles covering 45 marks, 7 → 6 while a member is focused.
  - ⛔ **Spreading along X is not on the menu.** The y-axis inside a swimlane carries no meaning to spend, which is why the fan can use it; x IS the meaning.
  - The two treatments are exclusive — a fanned lane has already separated its collisions, so the History tab is byte-identical (0–52px of logo antialiasing across four combinations).
- **ONE FACT, DRAWN, IS THE END OF ITS SENTENCE AND OF ITS BADGE.** (2026-09-02.) The dependencies tab's `Waiting on other services` card printed `hello-api-app` and `api 1.66.0` THREE times in one card: the subject line's `[API|1.66.0]` badge, the meta `Now on api 1.66.0, from rel-66`, and `BlockReason`'s drawn clause `⇄ hello-api-app [API|1.66.0] → [^1.67.0]`. The drawing is the one to keep, so the badge and the `Now on` clause are suppressed exactly when the clause draws, and the meta falls back to `From rel-66` — the one fact the drawing does not carry, in the form the mirror card already uses. ⛔ **The predicate mirrors `BlockReason`'s own `drawsVersions` exactly** (contract + served + required): where the relation cannot be drawn, the badge and the sentence must both come back or the served version is nowhere on the card. ⚠️ Residue: the provider is still named twice — once as the row's title (the object you open, and the only name when nothing is held) and once as the clause's left operand. Removing the second needs `BlockReason.svelte`.
- **THE SAME APP IN N ENVIRONMENTS IS ONE SUBJECT.** (2026-09-02.) `/dependencies`' banner mapped every held node through `nodeLabel` and joined, so one app held down one chain printed *"hello-frontend-app in dev, hello-frontend-app in staging, hello-frontend-app in prod"*. `heldSubjects` in `dependency-graph.ts` groups by app — the grouping is a property of the SENTENCE BUILDER, not of the banner, so nothing that says the same thing can drift from it. ⚠️ **A list whose items contain commas is separated by semicolons**: with `and` at both levels, `… staging and prod and hello-api-app in dev` reads as if `hello-api-app` were a fourth environment. The semicolon appears only in the mixed case. ⚠️ Order is the graph's and never alphabetical — the caller passes promotion order and that order is the story.
- When you discover a design constraint from user feedback, add it here immediately without waiting to be asked.

## Rollout list visual treatment

- No thickened or colored card borders. For status severity, use the dot indicator in the group header and the status dot in each row.

## The page container, and the vertical rhythm — one rule, measured

From the human (2026-09-01): *"pages have slightly different content margins so navigating
between pages feels jittery."* Measured at 1440 it was two separate defects.

**LATERAL — one content container for the whole product:**

```svelte
<div class="mx-auto w-full max-w-7xl px-4 py-6 sm:px-6">
```

1280px cap, 24px gutters (16px under `sm`). Content left edge **200px** at 1440 with the
sidebar open, **16px** at 390, on every route. **There are now NO exceptions.**

- **`w-full` is part of the recipe, not decoration.** `mx-auto` + `max-width` on a block
  parent and on a *flex* parent are not the same box: a flex item with `auto` cross-axis
  margins does not stretch, so it shrinks to its content. Dropped into the rollout layout
  (a flex column), the bare recipe rendered the Dependencies tab at **953px inside a
  1280px container** while its siblings measured 1280 — a page-width defect with no
  `max-w-*` anywhere near it. `w-full` makes the container's width independent of what its
  parent's `display` happens to be. It is a no-op under a block parent.
- ⛔ `/activity` was `max-w-5xl` — **976px against everyone else's 1216, a 128px jump on
  each side** on entry and exit. A narrower measure is legitimate ONLY when justified by
  LINE LENGTH; nothing on `/activity` is prose, so it was habit, not a reading measure.
- ⛔ Rollout detail's four tabs had **no wrapper at all** and four different paddings.
- ⛔ The Dependencies tab capped its own block at `max-w-[64rem]` one level *inside* a
  container that measured correctly.
- **If you add a page, use the recipe above.** A narrower `max-w-*` needs a line-length
  argument written next to it.

**⭐ THE TWO DEFECTS THAT SURVIVED THE FIRST PASS, AND WHY A CENSUS OF CONTAINER EDGES
CANNOT SEE EITHER.** (2026-09-02, from the human: *"rollout detail and environment list
still have larger margin than the rest of the pages. is it also the case somewhere
else?"* — *"still"*, one commit after the container was unified.) Measured first: at 1280,
1440, 1680, 1800 and 2560 in both themes, **`/environments` was byte-identical to every
other route** — container 372→1604 at 1800, first content block 372→1604, first card
372→…, trailing gap 0, and a column-ink-density profile denser than `/apps`'. The
container was never the thing. Two other mechanisms were:

1. **A full-bleed block INSIDE `<main>`.** Rollout detail's sticky tab strip was written
   down above as "the one documented exception". Its tabs sat at `px-2 sm:px-4`, i.e.
   16px from the pane edge, while the page under them sat in the container:

   | width | first tab box | content left | step |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | 1280 | 192 | 200 | **8** |
   | 1440 | 192 | 200 | **8** |
   | 1680 | 192 | 312 | **120** |
   | 1800 | 192 | 372 | **180** |
   | 2560 | 192 | 752 | **560** |

   It is the only page in the product that draws a reference line at the pane edge and
   then insets its content from it by a quarter of the viewport. **That step IS the
   "larger margin"** — the container was correct the whole time. The strip's background
   and bottom hairline stay full-bleed (they are chrome for the pane); its tab row is in
   the container now. **The tab BOX aligns with the content edge, not the tab LABEL** —
   the tab keeps `px-3`, exactly as a `Card`'s border sits at the block edge and its title
   16px inside. What aligns is the thing that draws a line: the active tab's `border-b-2`
   is a segment of the container's own left edge.

2. **A SECOND SCROLL CONTAINER, and the scrollbar it takes out of the content box.**
   ⭐ `mx-auto` centres in the **content** box, and a scroll container subtracts its
   scrollbar from that box. So on any platform with classic (non-overlay) scrollbars:
   - a page that **fits** the viewport is centred in `main`'s full width;
   - a page that **scrolls** is centred in `main` minus a scrollbar;
   - every edge on the short page therefore sits **half a scrollbar further out, on both
     sides**, than the same edge on the long page you just came from.

   Measured at 1800×950 on this cluster, `/environments`, `/` and a short rollout detail
   do not overflow `main`; `/apps`, `/versions`, `/activity`, `/envs/<name>` and
   `/rollouts` do. That is exactly the partition the human named. **`main` now carries
   `scrollbar-gutter: stable`**, so the content box is one width whether or not the page
   scrolls. It is a no-op where scrollbars are already overlays.

   ⛔ **AND A NESTED SCROLLER RESERVES A SECOND GUTTER.** Rollout detail owned its own
   `overflow-y-auto` pane, so with the gutter on it came out **357→1589 against everyone
   else's 364→1596** — the same defect, one level down, introduced by the fix for it. The
   pane is gone; rollout detail scrolls `<main>` like every other route and `sticky top-0`
   pins against `<main>`. Its Logs tab is `min-h-0 flex-1` instead of `h-full`, because
   `height: 100%` in a flex column that also holds a 49px tab strip is one tab strip too
   tall. **`/history` had the same shape at page level** — its container was itself
   `flex-1 overflow-y-auto`, i.e. the one container in the product that could eat its own
   right padding (24 left, 24 + a scrollbar right). It was also dead; its own
   `scrollToEntry` comment already records that the real scroller is four ancestors up.

   ⚠️ **THIS IS WHY TWO PASSES MEASURED THESE PAGES AND FOUND NOTHING.** Headless
   Chromium renders **overlay** scrollbars — `main.offsetWidth - main.clientWidth` was
   `0` on every route, so both mechanisms were literally zero-width in the instrument.
   If you are auditing lateral geometry, assert `scrollbar-gutter` is set rather than
   trusting a measured `0`.

**Ragged right is NOT a margin, and two pages have one on purpose.** `/rollouts` is
`grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 xl:grid-cols-3`, so a namespace group holding **2** rollouts
leaves one 405px track empty (trailing gap 355 at 1280, 413 at ≥1680). `/`'s last row
does the same with 8 cards in 3 columns. Both are a fixed grid's last row, not a
container defect — `auto-fit` would "fix" it by inflating a two-rollout group's cards to
616px, which is the inconsistency, not the cure. `/environments`' `.env-stack` is
`auto-fit` and fills exactly because its floor is derived from the card, not the row.

⭐ **NARROWED 2026-09-02 — TRUE OF ONE ROW, FALSE WHEN EVERY ROW IS THE LAST ROW.**
Measured on the live fleet (15 rollouts over 9 namespaces, so every group holds 1–2), the
empty share of `/rollouts`' card area was **44.8% at 1280, 44.7% at 1440, 44.7% at
1800** — nine groups, nine identical voids in the same place, under a group-header rule
that runs the full width. That is not a ragged last row; that is a promised region that
is half nothing. The rule now has a floor: **the grid may not open a track no group on
the page can fill.**
- ⛔ **SUPERSEDED THE SAME DAY.** The 460px-capped fix below was measured
  again a few hours later and found to have traded the hole for a margin:
  `460px 460px` in a 1201px container is **76.6%** used and a one-rollout
  namespace's single `460px` track is **38.3%** — better than 45% empty but
  still short of "fills its container." The auto-fill/auto-fit rejections
  below were also re-examined: `auto-fill` genuinely reopens the 44.8% hole
  (it keeps empty trailing tracks at their floor), but `auto-fit` does NOT —
  it collapses a track with nothing in it to 0 and lets the occupied
  tracks' `1fr` absorb the freed space, which is exactly `.env-stack`'s own
  mechanism one line up. The card-inflation argument against equal columns
  (~596px, badge halves separating by ~460px) is real but is a SECOND-ORDER
  cosmetic complaint against a FIRST-ORDER "the row is 62–77% empty" one,
  and loses. **Current: `xl:[grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fit,minmax(360px,1fr))]`,
  per group (no JS cap needed — each namespace's own grid decides its own
  track count from its own card count), verified ≥95% used-width at 1440 on
  every group on the live fleet.** See `RolloutGrid.svelte`'s own note for
  the full account; the bullets below are kept as the historical record of
  what was tried and why, not as the current rule.
- `RolloutGrid`'s track COUNT is `min(3, largest group)` and its track WIDTH is capped at
  **460px** so cards cannot inflate. On this fleet 45% → **26 / 36 / 37%**; on any fleet
  where a namespace holds three or more the class string is **byte-identical** to before.
- ⛔ **`auto-fill` with the card's real minimum is WORSE, and it was measured.** The
  card's `max-content` is **264px** (everything inside truncates), so `minmax(264px, 1fr)`
  opens FOUR tracks at 1201 and a two-rollout group goes to **50% empty**. Auto-fill
  answers "how many fit"; the question is "how many are there".
- ⛔ **Two EQUAL columns is the `auto-fit` defect by another route.** Cards go to 596px
  against 264px of content, so the badge row's two facts (`[NEWEST|…]` and `4d ago
  updated`) separate by ~460px and stop reading as one card.
- ⛔ **The cap is on `xl` only.** Between 640 and 1279 the grid is already two tracks and
  a two-rollout group already fills it; capping there would INVENT a void.
- Verified: at 390 the diff is **0 pixels** (light) / 24 (logo antialiasing, dark); at
  1440 the card's padding, radius, border, background, shadow, gap and height are
  identical and every left-anchored child sits at the same offset from the card origin —
  only `width` and the five right-anchored spans move, by exactly the 65px delta.

**VERTICAL — the head band is chrome and is identical everywhere:**

```
y=0    the container's `py-6`
y=24   THE HEAD ROW — one row: a 24px lead (`t-display`, `t-display-id`, or a 24px
       object name with `leading-[1.15]`) and, on its baseline, the page's rollup at
       `t-dense`.  `flex flex-wrap items-baseline gap-x-2 gap-y-1`, height 28px.
y=52   `mb-5` — 20px, never `mb-4` or `mb-6`
y=72   THE FIRST CONTENT ELEMENT, on every page.
```

Only genuine CONTENT may push a page below y=72 — a banner, a filter bar, a definition
sentence long enough to wrap. Chrome may not. Before this rule the first content element
ranged **62 → 98** at 1440 on pages with nothing above it; it is 72 on all of them now.
`/` is the one page with no head band at all (standing constraint: it does not change
visually) — its first ink is still at y=24.

At 390 the head row WRAPS, so its height is set by the rollup's own length. That is content,
not chrome: the 24px above it and the 20px below it are identical at every width.

⛔ **AND THE RHYTHM BELONGS TO EVERY BRANCH OF THE PAGE, NOT JUST THE LOADED ONE.**
(2026-09-02) Rollout detail's loading skeleton and its 404 both carried `py-8` while its
loaded state carried `pt-6 pb-10`, so the head row **moved down 8px the moment the data
arrived** — a rhythm defect that only exists for one frame and is therefore never
screenshotted. `/rollouts/…/diff/<version>` was `py-8` outright, 32px against everyone
else's 24. All four are `pt-6` now. When you touch a container, grep the file for its
`{#if loading}` and `{:else if error}` siblings.
